Trade re-routed, not destroyed: Asian exports to Africa and South America
Risks: a long Hormuz closure, tariff payback, an AI slowdown
theory: UNCTAD: containerised trade +2.3% a year in 2026–2030. BIMCO 2027 ship demand: +0.5–2.5% if Hormuz stays closed, +2.5–4.5% if it reopens, against fleet growth of about 9%.
case: Hapag-Lloyd: volumes −0.7% in Q1 2026 (weather, Hormuz) and +1.5% in H1; Jebel Ali about −30% in Q1.
speakerNotes: Built from the Req 2 script (no slide text given). Maersk assumes about 4% market growth for 2026. Drewry: a long Hormuz closure could cut 2026 growth to 0.5-1.3%. All numbers need sources.
